Still drawings computed from joint angles, in the app's own colours: no photos, no video. Tap Trace to play the path once, Mistake to see the common fault, and a label to highlight its cue.

App theme

LB5

How to do itPreacher Curl

Sit with the pad top under your armpits and your chest on it.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Arms off padYour upper arms lift off the pad as you heave the bar.
  2. Torso heaves backYour torso rocks back off the pad to swing the bar up.
Curl1 s
Lower2 s

How to do itCable Curl

Keep the elbows close to your torso. Never let the upper arms go back.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Arms locked straightYour arms go fully straight at the bottom, so the biceps lose tension.
Lower2 s
Curl1 s

How to do itBayesian Cable Curl

Start with the working arm drawn back behind your torso, cable taut.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Upper arm swingsYour upper arm swings forward so the shoulder helps lift the handle.
Curl1 s
Lower2 s

How to do itConcentration Curl

Brace the back of your upper arm on the inner thigh, not the knee.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbow in kneeYour elbow is wedged into the knee instead of the arm on the thigh.
Curl1 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s

How to do itDumbbell Overhead Triceps Extension

Keep the upper arms vertical and still. Only the elbows bend.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Back archesYour lower back arches as you press the dumbbell up.
Press1 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s

How to do itCross-Body Hammer Curl

Keep a neutral grip, palms toward you, with no wrist twist.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Shoulder shrugsYour working shoulder hikes up toward your ear as the dumbbell rises.
Curl1 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s

How to do itWrist Curl

Rest the forearm on your thigh. Only the hand moves.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Body leans inYour body leans forward to help move the weight.
  2. Arm straightensYour arm straightens and the forearm lifts off the thigh.
Curl2 s
Lower2 s

How to do itHammer Curl

Keep the palms facing your body from bottom to top. No wrist twist.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbows forwardYour elbows move forward as the dumbbells come up.
  2. Shoulder takes overThe front of your shoulder takes the load instead of the biceps.
Curl1 s
Lower2 s

How to do itAlternating Dumbbell Curl

Keep the resting arm hanging in the start position.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbow swingsYour working elbow swings forward off your side.
Curl1 s
Lower2 s

How to do itSingle-Arm Triceps Pushdown

Keep the working upper arm at your side so only the forearm moves.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Leaning overYou lean over the handle or arch your back to push it down.
Press1 s
Hold1 s
Return2 s

How to do itIncline Dumbbell Curl

Set the bench high but not upright, about 45 to 65 degrees.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbows forwardYour elbows drift forward as the dumbbells rise.
  2. Arm comes forwardThe arm comes forward and the biceps lose stretch and tension.
Curl1 s
Lower2 s

How to do itStraight-Bar Triceps Pushdown

Keep the upper arms close to your sides. Only the forearms move.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Leaning overYou lean far over the bar or arch your back to push it down.
Press1 s
Hold1 s
Return2 s

How to do itBarbell Curl

Keep the upper arms by your body. Never let them travel back.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbows backYour elbows travel back behind you to cheat the bar up.
Curl1 s
Lower2 s

How to do itEZ-Bar Curl

Keep the elbows close to your body. Do not let them drift forward on top.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Elbows forwardYour elbows drift forward as the bar reaches the top.
Curl1 s
Hold1 s
Lower2 s

How to do itReverse Curl

Hold the bar overhand about shoulder-width and keep that grip all the way up.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Body swingsYour body rocks back to swing the bar up.
Curl1 s
Lower2 s
